name: flagstone temple court ground autotile: large irregular pale limestone slabs with dark joints, moss in the joints, a cracked and a sunken slab, a low dressed kerb rim with a 2px front face on the south edge, lying flat on grass (top-down 3/4 RPG ground)
label: beodeul_yard/flag

surfaces.part: flagstone paving field (irregular slabs, joints, moss, cracked and sunken slab)
dressed kerb rim along the south edges, 2px front face with a light top line and a dark joint line below

answer.evidence: The tile is flat ground seen from above. The slabs, joints and moss are all drawn as one horizontal paving plane, and the column scans show only slab and joint bands. The only vertical face is the low kerb. Its front face is 2 rows (a light line like #f2ead8 over a dark joint like #686048) on the south edges, which is under the 3-row minimum for a front face. There is no receding side face and no eave or roof. The shape is a flat slab on grass with only a thin kerb lip.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 16 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass reference. Near-flat coverage is 3%, close to the references' 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The slabs show about 5 steps (cream highlight, light, mid, shadow, dark joint), with per-slab edge highlights and grey wedge shading on the cracked and sunken slabs. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the joints and kerb outline are tinted brown-olive rather than black, which reads as dark material tone. The kerb has a lit top and a darker 2px south face, and it separates by value. Weaknesses: the grass outside the paving has only sparse tufts and is plainer than the Beodeul grass, the moss in the joints is faint, and the slabs read as smallish cobbles. None of this makes it look like a flat sticker beside the references, so it holds up as a careful, richly shaded ground piece.

surfaces.part: flagstone paving field with moss joints, cracked and sunken slabs
dressed kerb rim along the south edges

answer.evidence: The paving is a flat top-down ground autotile that fills nearly the whole 144-row canvas, an irregular patch with a grass hole and a small separate block. The only vertical face is the kerb's 2px south face, visible at the bottom edge of each paved section. That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face. The rest is flat slab texture with dark joints, so it reads as a top-down slab, which is normal for terrain. There is no standing volume, eave or ellipse.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 16 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is only 3%, so large flat fills are not a problem. The slabs show about 5 lightness steps: pale highlight, cream, mid tan, shadow tan and dark joint. Each stone is shaded individually, with small grey facets in the cracked or sunken slabs. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the joints and kerb outline lean brown-tan rather than black. The kerb has a lit top edge and a darker south face, which matches the selective, material-tone outlining of the reference. The surrounding grass is a low-contrast but textured tuft pattern, comparable to the grass reference. Weaknesses: the slabs read as smaller than the 'large irregular' brief, and the moss in the joints is sparse. Neither is a style-depth failure, and the piece would sit acceptably beside the references.

surfaces.part: flagstone paving field (flat ground slabs with joints, moss, cracked and sunken slab)
low dressed kerb rim along the edges, with a 2px front face on the south edges

answer.evidence: The candidate is a ground autotile: a large flat area of irregular pale limestone slabs with dark joints, seen almost straight down. It has no standing body, ellipse, roof or eave. The only vertical element is a kerb rim with a 2-row front face along the south edges, for example near the bottom of the lower-right block. That is under 3 rows, so there is no real front face. The column scans show repeating slab, joint and highlight rows across the whole height, which means a flat paving pattern and not a top plus front-face structure. The grass area inside the courtyard is flat ground, not a raised top. The piece reads as a top-down slab, as expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 16 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 3%, so there are no large flat areas. The paving has cream highlights, mid tones, shadowed edges and dark brown-tinted joints, with moss tufts in the joints and shaded triangular chips on individual stones. The 0% neutral share of dark edge pixels means the outlines and joints lean brown rather than black, matching the dark-material-tone approach. The kerb rim has a lit top and a darker south face. The grass outside the paving carries tuft grain. The ramps (about 5 steps) are slightly shallower than Beodeul's 5-6, and the slabs read smaller and more cobble-like than 'large' slabs, but neither is a style failure. A careful artist would accept it next to the references.

surfaces.part: flagstone paving field with moss joints, cracked and sunken slabs
low dressed kerb rim, south edge front face

answer.evidence: The tile is a flat, irregular paving field seen from above. The slabs, joints, moss and cracks all lie in one horizontal plane, and the outline is an irregular autotile shape on grass with a grass hole inside. The only vertical face is the kerb on the south edges, about 2 rows of light face under a dark joint line (for example column x=131 rows 34-36). That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face, so the drawing has no real front face and counts as a flat top-down slab, which is the normal form for ground terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 16 visible tones per full tile against 3 for the reference grass and 7 for the reference paving. Near-flat coverage is 3%, close to the references' 0%. Each slab is shaded individually with a light face, mid tone and darker edge. Joints are a warm brown-grey, and 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark material tone rather than a black sticker line. Details include cracks, a sunken slab, and moss tufts in the joints. The kerb has a dressed rim with a 2px south face, and the grass surround carries subtle tufts. The ramp is slightly shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material, since the slabs are mostly 4-5 limestone steps. The overall craft and information density still match the references and read as the same style.
